method.method_draft: Use area decomposition inside triangle ABF. Let vectors from B be BA=a and BF=f. Since F is the midpoint of BC and ABCD is a square, D=a+2f and E=a/2. A point on AF can be written as (1-t)a+tf, where t is the fraction of the way from A to F. For H, because H lies on BD, write H=s(a+2f) and equate coefficients with (1-t)a+tf; this gives t=2/3, so FH/AF=1/3. For I, because I lies on ED, write I=E+r(D-E)=a/2+r(a/2+2f) and equate with (1-t)a+tf; this gives t=2/5, so AI/AF=2/5. Now triangle ABF has area (1/2)(AB)(BF)=(1/2)(2)(1)=1. The quadrilateral BEIH is triangle ABF minus triangles AEI and BFH. Since E is the midpoint of AB, [AEI]/[ABF]=(AE/AB)(AI/AF)=(1/2)(2/5)=1/5. Also [BFH]/[ABF]=FH/AF=1/3. Therefore [BEIH]=1-1/5-1/3=7/15.
